text:
carmen: FYI getting multiple customer reports of 503s and huge p50/p95 latency on hosted inference for tenant 'acme-payments'. Started ~09:02 UTC. Link: https://observability.redwood/example/trace/abcd1234
incident-bot: Alert: high-error-rate detected for model=gpt-infer-v3 pool=hosted-gpu-3 - 503s increased to 7% over 5m
jordan: can you paste the trace id? I'll check upstream runners
carmen: trace id abcd1234, sample span shows runner pod returning exit code 137 repeatedly
maya: looking at node and pod logs now, kubelet shows container killed by OOM killer; kernel oom messages present
alex: here's a clipped pod log sample:
```
I0312 09:01:59.112 INFO  runtime starting request id=abcd req_len=1200 model=gpt-infer-v3
W0312 09:02:16.987 WARN  gpu_allocator cublas allocation failed: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED
I0312 09:02:17.005 INFO  runner buffering batch size=32 total_tokens=12000
E0312 09:02:17.234 ERROR runtime: runtime: out of memory
Killed process 4211 (infer-runner) total-vm:124000000kB, anon-rss:98000000kB, file-rss:0kB
```
maya: exit code 137 -> SIGKILL, looks like system-level OOM. Some traces show cublas failing before the kill which may have led to retrying and accumulating memory
jordan: do we see a traffic pattern? long contexts or large batch sizes?
carmen: customer reports a handful of requests with very long context windows (max_tokens up to 9k) around the period. They also reported a spike in billed tokens which triggered the support escalation
maya: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) divert acme-payments to the quantized-fallback pool 2) enforce a temporary max_tokens cap for hosted requests > 4096 3) schedule scale-up of dedicated nodes for burst traffic
alex: quick repro we ran locally:
```
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-infer-v3","input":"<very large prompt>","max_tokens":9000}'
# observe pod mem climb and exit with code 137 in ~18-25s
```
jordan: I'm spinning up one 80GB-GPU node to the hosted pool to relieve pressure and rebalancing the routing tables now
maya: also enable nv-profiling on one repro pod and collect dmesg & /var/log/kern.log for the timeframe. We should capture cuda driver messages and any allocation failures prior to OOM
carmen: I've informed the customer of temporary throttling and that we're putting a safe-fallback in place. They've accepted temporary cap while we investigate
alex: logging note: we saw a subtle batching bug where a failed cublas allocation triggered a retry path that appended partial KV cache entries without freeing leading to accumulation
maya: next actions: (A) root-cause collect + trace of memory growth, (B) patch retry path to free partial state on allocation failures, (C) create remediation playbook to auto-fallback long-context requests to quantized model or rate-limit
carmen: assigning INC-2026 to maya/jordan/alex. paging oncall now
incident-bot: Pager: paging maya via #oncall - escalation level 1
maya: acked, taking lead. I'll post updates and a short postmortem when we have RCA
carmen: thanks all :thumbsup:
